name: Dumbbell Shrug
description: The dumbbell shrug is a trapezius isolation exercise where dumbbells are held at the sides and the shoulders are elevated (shrugged) upward toward the ears. The upper trapezius is the primary mover responsible for scapular elevation. Dumbbells allow a natural path of motion and can be rotated during the shrug for a variation that also engages the mid-trapezius.

execution.starting_position: Stand upright holding a dumbbell in each hand at the sides, arms fully extended. Feet shoulder-width apart. Shoulders are in a neutral, depressed position.
execution.setup_instructions: Select appropriately heavy dumbbells. Stand tall with good posture before beginning.
steps: Step 1: Hold dumbbells at the sides with arms fully extended. Stand tall, shoulders neutral.
Step 2: Exhale and elevate both shoulders straight upward toward the ears as high as possible.
Step 3: Hold the peak shrug for 1 second.
Step 4: Inhale and lower the shoulders back to the starting neutral position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the shrug upward; inhale on the return.
common_mistakes: Rolling the shoulders forward or backward — shrug straight up, not in a circle
Using heavy weight that reduces range of motion — prioritize full elevation
safety_considerations: Keep the neck long — do not let the head jut forward as the shoulders rise
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Elevate fully to the ears; return to fully depressed and neutral position.
coaching_cues: Shrug straight up — not forward, not back, not in a circle
Feel the traps 'peaking' at the top of each rep
